name: Sonde
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Koni Muluwa, Joseph & Koen Bostoen. 2015. Lexique comparé des langues bantu du Kwilu (République démocratique du Congo). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe (publisher page)
sources.note: Publisher page names the covered groups (B80, L10 Pende/Kwese/Saamba, H40 Mbala/Hungan, H30 Suku); Soonde is not named, so this work is not a Sonde source.
Nothing; cites only Ethnologue and Maho 2009; notes two Sondes (H321 near Suku, L101 near Pende) not distinguished by ISO.

sources.citation: Maho, Jouni Filip. 2009. NUGL Online: The online version of the New Updated Guthrie List, a referential classification of the Bantu languages (4 June 2009). Internet Archive copy of goto.glocalnet.net/mahopapers/
sources.note: Nothing; classification only. p.55 'H321 So(o)nde shc, Kisonde' (Suku group); p.68 'L101 Sonde' (Pende group); p.54 'H16e Bwende, incl. Sonde' (a Kongo variety, a different Sonde).

sources.citation: Bastin, Yvonne, A. Coupez & Michael Mann. 1999. Continuity and divergence in the Bantu languages: perspectives from a lexicostatistic study. Tervuren: MRAC. (Soonde list reused in Grollemund et al. 2015 / lexibank-grollemundbantu, held by the project)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the Tervuren Soonde wordlist (h321soonde) carries high-tone marks (e.g. méénga 'blood', táŋgá 'count', kwíza 'come'), i.e. Sonde was recorded as a tone language; no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald et al. Glottolog 5.3, languoid record sond1250 (JSON) and reference records 98100 (Bilongo Bweya 1972) and 71905 (Diata 1981)
sources.note: Nothing; the record lists Glottolog's most extensive descriptions Bilongo Bweya 1972 (rank phonology or text collection) and Torday & Joyce 1907 (a wordlist or less); no grammar or phonology exists in Glottolog for this language.

sources.citation: Torday, Emil & T. Athol Joyce. 1907. On the ethnology of the south-western Congo Free State. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 37: 133-156 (archive.org SIM microfilm scan of vol. 37, scanned text)
sources.note: Nothing; an ethnological survey of Kwilu peoples (Ba-Samba, Ba-Songo, Wa-Ngongo, Ba-Yaka, Ba-Mbala, Ba-Huana, etc.); the scanned contains no 'Sonde'/'Basonde' and no vocabulary table.

sources.citation: Diata, M. 1981. Étude descripto-comparative des démonstratifs soonde (H56), suku (H32) et mbala (H41). Mémoire, UNILU Lubumbashi.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Second of only two descriptive works on Sonde in Glottolog; may have a short phonological note on the Soonde demonstrative forms (tone).

sources.citation: Bilongo Bweya, N'zemba-Baala. 1972. Essai d'une morphologie comparée des formes nominales et pronominales des langues Sonde et Ngongo: contribution à la classification des langues. Mémoire, UNAZA Lubumbashi, vii+113 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description of Sonde (Glottolog's most extensive description rank phonology or text collection); a 113-page comparative morphology thesis is the only work likely to contain a phonological preliminary (tone/accent) for Sonde.

sources.citation: Any sociolinguistic or phonological survey of the Kwilu/Kwango H30 languages by SIL-Congo or BantUGent (Bostoen and colleagues) that includes Soonde (none identified; sil.org resource page for shc could not be reached by automated download)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: BantUGent has produced phonological work on neighbouring Kwilu languages (Mbuun, Nsong, Hungan, Mbala); a Soonde item, if any, would be the first modern description.
